**Play:**

2. Keep Quake (#31) and both Soldier tokens home. The tokens are summoning sick and can't attack anyway.
3. Your 2 Plains stay untapped, but you have nothing to cast at instant speed. Robotics Mastery costs 5, and Spy Kit is a sorcery-speed artifact.

**Why:** The opponent has no flyers, and their Helicarrier can't be crewed. Their creatures have total power 0 (-3 + 2 + 1), and Crew 6 needs 6. They are fully tapped out with no hand, so Doombot is a free 1 damage. Quake attacking into the 2/2 and 1/1 risks a double block: 2 + 1 = 3 damage kills Quake, and you'd trade your best creature for two tokens. Lethal isn't close either way (20 life each, and their board has about 3 power).

**Rule:** Take free damage, don't risk your engine in a bad trade.

**Confidence:** High.

**Trap:** Attacking with Quake as well. A 3/3 looks like it beats their small blockers, but a double block kills it. Quake also pays off later when you cast noncreature spells (it taps a creature or land).

**Their turn:** They have Soldiers 2/2 and 1/1, plus Peggy at -3 power, so they have at most 3 power to attack with. Quake and your two Soldier tokens can block. They untap 5 lands with no hand, so they only have a topdeck. Doombot being tapped doesn't matter.

**Alternative:** None that is close.

ANSWER: attack:25

1. Block Giant-Sized Flying Ant #64 (3/2 flier) with Ant-Man's Air Force #23. #23 is your only flier, and its 2 damage kills the Ant.
2. Block Quake #71 (3/3) with Quake #31. They trade.
3. Block Agent Phil Coulson #70 (2/2) with Agent Phil Coulson #30. They trade.
4. Leave Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. #50 (2/4) unblocked. You take 2 and go to 4.
5. Cast nothing. Thriving Isle is your only untapped land and makes U or B. Helicarrier Strike needs {W}, so it can't be cast.

**Why:** At 6 life, 10 power is attacking, so you must block. Blocking three attackers means you take at most 3 damage, and the unblocked 2/4 is the weakest one to let through. Every block is an even or favorable trade, and it kills their Ant, their Quake and their Coulson (which pumps their other Heroes). Take 2 from #50 and you stay at 4.

**Rule:** Count lethal, then trade on your terms. Stay out of burst range first, then make even trades.

**Confidence:** Medium. Blocking all three so the damage taken stays small is clearly right. Which trades to take is close.

**Trap:** Blocking only two attackers. That looks cheaper, but it leaves you at 1 life (taking 5) and dead to any trick, flash flier or pump. Blocking #50 with #30 is also bad: the 2/2 dies and the 2/4 survives.

**Their turn:** They have 6 untapped lands and 3 hidden cards. They could use a trick on a blocked creature, or cast a noncreature spell to trigger Quake #71 (which taps a creature or land) after blockers. After combat you likely have no creatures, and they keep #50 and anything cast post-combat. Next turn, rebuild blockers with Strategic Intervention, Helicarrier Strike mana held up, or other plays, and keep W open for Strike.

**Alternative:** Block #70 with #31 (Coulson dies, #31 survives), #71 with nobody, #30 on #50. This keeps #31 alive but leaves you at 3 life with their Quake still on board. It's slightly worse.

ANSWER: block:23>64,31>71,30>70

1. Play a land. Thriving Isle is the best pick: it enters tapped, you choose White, and it gives U or W from next turn on. You only have 1 Plains untapped, so a tapped land costs you nothing this turn.
2. Cast nothing. Your only untapped source is the Plains (W), and you can't afford any spell with it. Bold Biochemist and Quantum Reduction both need {U}, and Quake needs 3 mana.
3. No attack, since you have no creatures. Mana left at the end: W unused.

**Why:** It's turn 3 for you but you only have one land on the battlefield, so you've missed drops. Playing Thriving Isle tapped now sets up turn 2 with Plains + Isle (U/W), which can cast Biochemist. After that, Quake comes down with a third land.

**Rule:** Use your tapped land on the turn you can't spend the mana anyway.

**Confidence:** high

**Trap:** Playing Island untapped looks like it enables Biochemist, but with Plains + Island that's only 2 mana and a 1/3 body now. It's also the wrong order for your hand. Playing Island lets you cast Biochemist this turn, but you'd then have to play the tapped land on a later turn, which costs you tempo then. Check: Plains untapped + Island untapped = {W}{U}, which does pay {1}{U}. So this is a real alternative, see below.

**Their turn:** They have an Aerial Doombot, a 1/1 flier that will no longer be summoning sick, so expect 1 damage in the air. They have 6 cards in hand and will untap with 2 lands. Nothing you hold needs to be kept back.

**Alternative:** Play Island and cast Bold Biochemist {1}{U} (Plains pays generic, Island pays U). This gives you a 1/3 body now, and you play Thriving Isle tapped next turn, leaving you with 2 usable lands next turn and only 3 on the turn after. That's actually the stronger tempo line: you use all your mana this turn. Playing Thriving Isle now wastes this turn's mana, while the Island line spends it. Next turn you'd have Plains + Island untapped plus a tapped Thriving Isle, so Quake would wait until the turn after. In the Thriving line, next turn is Plains + Isle + a new untapped land = 3 mana for Quake. So Thriving first gets Quake a turn earlier, while Island first gets Biochemist a turn earlier.

Since I wrongly claimed nothing was castable above, correcting: the Island line is a real option and I now prefer it, because a 1/3 blocker is cheap but real board presence, and it uses mana this turn.

**Corrected Play:**
1. Play Island (untapped).
2. Cast Bold Biochemist {1}{U}: Plains pays {1}, Island pays {U}. Mana left: none.
3. No attacks.

Next turn: play Thriving Isle tapped and cast nothing big, or play Plains and cast Quake with 3 lands, then Thriving Isle after. Quake on turn 3-of-yours-onward works with Plains, Island, Plains.

**Confidence:** medium. The two lines are close; Island plus Biochemist uses all your mana now and still gets Quake out next turn by playing Plains.

ANSWER: cast:12
